input.quote: Upon reasonable request not more than once during any calendar year, and with reasonable notice, the Servicer will give the Issuer, the Depositor, the Parent Support Provider, the Administrator, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee (or their representatives) access to the records and documents to conduct a review of the Servicer's performance under this Agreement.
input.rationale: No audit, inspection or verification right in this Agreement binds us. Every review right runs in our favour against the counterparty: Section 3.6 (p0131) gives the Issuer, Depositor and related parties access to the Servicer's records once per calendar year on reasonable notice, at the Servicer's offices during normal business hours; Section 3.4(e) (p0146) gives the Depositor, Issuer and Indenture Trustee access to the Custodian's Receivable Files; Section 6.6/6.7 (p0302-p0312) require the Servicer's annual compliance statement, Regulation AB servicing assessment and an independent accountants' attestation delivered to us; and Article XI (p0441-p0447) obliges the Servicer to support an Asset Representations Review by an independent Asset Representations Reviewer, with Personally Identifiable Information redacted. Because the AUDIT rule targets audits of our usage and no such right exists against us (and none grants the counterparty access to our systems), the position is better than preferred and we do not redline. Noted only in passing: the Servicer-side review right is framed as "once during any calendar year" on "reasonable notice" rather than a fixed 30-day notice period, but that runs against the counterparty and is to our benefit.
